Subject: Embeddings model fit validation \u0014 post-demo recap

Hi Emma / Daniel,

Thanks for taking the time today \u0014 great conversation and appreciated the context on the catalog search use cases and SKU-level synonyms. Quick recap from our side and recommended next steps: 

- What we heard as the highest priority: improve semantic recall for short queries (1-3 tokens) and surface closest SKUs for fuzzy match and synonyms; reduce false positives where color/size attributes mismatch.
- Recommended models to validate (initial sweep): redwood-emb-small-v2 (768d) for latency-sensitive prototypes, redwood-emb-large-v1 (1536d) for highest-fidelity recall.
- Initial benchmark highlights (attached CSV): our internal eval on a 10k-sku sample showed MRR 0.62 / Recall@10 0.88 for large model; small model MRR 0.55 / Recall@10 0.81. Distance metric: cosine; suggested cutoffs: 0.75+ for strong match, 0.6-0.75 ambiguous.
- Dimensionality tradeoffs: 1536d generally gives higher recall on subtle semantic differences; 768d often hits an excellent throughput/latency sweet spot with modest recall loss. We recommend running both on a representative shard of your catalog.
- Drift & regression concerns: we flagged a 4-month drift case in a different retail customer where embeddings drifted ~6% in average pairwise cosine over time due to seasonal product titles \u0014 we'll include a small drift-detection prompt set for baseline.

Next steps / POC plan we propose:
1) Atlas provides a 10-20k representative SKU sample + a holdout query set (we can provide a template).
2) Redwood runs parallel evaluation on redwood-emb-small-v2 and redwood-emb-large-v1, returns metrics (MRR, Recall@1/5/10, latency p50/p95) and qualitative failure cases.
3) Joint review and calibration session (30-45m) to pick candidate model for the integration POC.

I've attached: atlas_poc_scope.pdf (POC scope & timeline), embedding_benchmarks_20270215.csv (sample eval), and prompt_set_v1.txt (suggested query/label template). Also sharing a Drive folder with the full eval harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-embeddings-eval

Thanks \u0014 happy to sync or jump on a call to walk through the CSV.

Emma / Daniel \u0014 quick answers, plus some practical recommendations: 

1) Latency: on our reference infra a 768d embedding lookup + FAISS HNSW index p95 (search only) is ~35-60ms; 1536d is ~65-110ms. When you include retrieval + business logic (filtering by attributes) you can expect higher. With 200-300 QPS we recommend batching and a dedicated ANN tier (HNSW with sharding) \u0014 that keeps p95 comfortably under 200ms in our experience. We can share concrete perf numbers if you give us a representative payload size.
2) Query type: the CSV includes both exact-title and intentionally noisy/typo queries; the MRR/Recall numbers are aggregated. We can break those out separately in the next run. For short/typo-heavy queries the larger model tends to recover more correct results but the gap narrows when you add a shallow lexical rerank + fuzzy matching.
3) Data sharing: sanitized CSV is fine to start. If you prefer S3 read-only access we can sign an MFA-protected temporary role; both work. For security/compliance: we can send the standard questionnaire and an SOC2 evidence bundle as needed.

Recommendation: start with a dual-path POC \u0014 run 10k through both dims, capture MRR and recall by query-type, and add a small lexicographic reranker. We'll deliver a short summary and top-20 failure cases.

Attaching the POC scope and prompt set again for convenience.
